Amounts are integer cents, negative for outflow.\r\nEach account has a transfer payee that stands for it. The budget is the envelope budget. Every rule holds for\r\nany number of lines in one import and any number of transactions in one change.\r\n\r\n## Modules and entry points\r\n\r\n| Module | Where | Entry points |\r\n|---|---|---|\r\n| Transactions | `src/server/transactions/index.ts` | `batchUpdateTransactions({ added, updated, deleted })` |\r\n| Transfers | `src/server/transactions/transfer.ts` | Called by the transactions module |\r\n| Statement import | `src/server/accounts/sync.ts` | `reconcileTransactions(accountId, lines)`, handler `transactions-import` |\r\n| Rules | `src/server/transactions/transaction-rules.ts`, `src/server/rules/` | `insertRule`, `loadRules`, `runRules` |\r\n| Schedules | `src/server/schedules/app.ts` | `createSchedule`, handler `schedule/post-transaction`. In tests, start the schedules app's services first, as `schedules/app.test.ts` does. |\r\n| Merge | `src/server/transactions/merge.ts` | `mergeTransactions([{ id }, { id }])`, handler `transactions-merge` |\r\n| Envelope budget | `src/server/budget/` | Month sheet `budgetYYYYMM`, cell `sum-amount-<categoryId>` |\r\n\r\nA statement line passed to `reconcileTransactions` has `date`, `amount`, `payee_name`, and optionally `imported_id`,\r\n`notes` and `category`.\r\n\r\n## T. Transfers\r\n\r\n- **T1.** A transaction whose payee is another account's transfer payee is a transfer. It has exactly one\r\n  counterpart in that account, created with the opposite amount, the same date and the first account's transfer\r\n  payee. Each side references the other through `transfer_id`.\r\n- **T2.** T1 holds however the payee was set: entered directly, set by a rule, set during a statement import, or\r\n  posted by a schedule.\r\n- **T3.** Changing the amount of either side sets the other side to the opposite amount. Changing the notes of\r\n  either side copies them to the other. Changing the date of one side does not change the other.\r\n- **T4.** Changing a side's payee to a different account's transfer payee moves the counterpart to that account.\r\n  Changing it to a regular payee deletes the counterpart. Deleting either side deletes the other.\r\n- **T5.** Between two on-budget accounts, or two off-budget accounts, neither side has a category.\r\n- **T6.** From an on-budget account to an off-budget account, the on-budget side keeps its category and counts as\r\n  activity in that category. The counterpart is created without a category.\r\n\r\n## A. Accounts and categories\r\n\r\n- **A1.** Adding a transaction to an off-budget account, or moving one into it, clears its category.\r\n- **A2.** Transactions in off-budget accounts never count toward budget activity.\r\n\r\n## I. Statement import\r\n\r\n- **I0.** A line's `payee_name` is title-cased (`GROCER outlet` becomes `Grocer Outlet`) and kept as the imported\r\n  payee. It names an existing payee whose name is equal ignoring case; otherwise a new payee is created.\r\n- **I1.** Rules run on each line before it is matched, so a rule can set the line's payee, category or notes.\r\n- **I2.** A line whose `imported_id` equals the `imported_id` of a transaction in the same account is that\r\n  transaction.\r\n- **I3.** Otherwise a line matches a transaction in the same account with the same amount, dated at most 7 days\r\n  before or after the line, that no other line of the same import has matched. When the line has an\r\n  `imported_id`, only transactions without an `imported_id` qualify. Any qualifying transaction can be matched,\r\n  including one side of a transfer. Matching runs in two passes over the whole import. First, in line order,\r\n  each line takes the nearest qualifying candidate whose payee equals the line's payee as set after rules ran.\r\n  Then, in line order, each line still unmatched takes the nearest qualifying candidate left. When two candidates\r\n  are equally near, either may be taken.\r\n- **I4.** A matched line adds nothing. The matched transaction keeps its own payee, category and notes, and empty\r\n  ones are filled from the line after rules ran, in any account, off-budget accounts included. The transaction's\r\n  `imported_id` becomes the line's `imported_id`, or none when the line has none. A transfer side stays a transfer\r\n  side, and T5 and T6 decide its category. A matched transaction that is reconciled is left unchanged.\r\n- **I5.** An unmatched line is added to the account. A1 and T1 to T6 apply to it.\r\n\r\n## R. Rules\r\n\r\n- **R1.** A rule condition `contains` on `imported_payee` compares case-insensitively with the line's payee text.\r\n- **R2.** A rule action `set` on `payee` or `category` sets that field on the matching line.\r\n- **R3.** Rules run on statement lines, on transactions posted by a schedule, and on a new transfer counterpart,\r\n  where only their notes and cleared status take effect. They do not run on transactions passed to\r\n  `batchUpdateTransactions`.\r\n\r\n## S. Schedules\r\n\r\n- **S1.** A schedule names an account, a payee, an amount and a date or recurrence. Posting its transaction\r\n  creates a transaction on the schedule's next date with that account, payee and amount, linked to the schedule\r\n  through its `schedule` field. Posting does not change the schedule's next date, and posting again creates\r\n  another transaction.\r\n- **S2.** When the schedule's payee is a transfer payee, posting creates the transfer, and both sides are linked to\r\n  the schedule.\r\n\r\n## M. Merge\r\n\r\n- **M1.** Merging two transactions of the same account with the same amount keeps one: the one with an\r\n  `imported_id` when only one has one; otherwise the one with an imported payee when only one has one; otherwise\r\n  the one with the earlier date, or the second one given when the dates are equal. Empty payee, category and\r\n  notes of the kept transaction are filled from the other, and the other is deleted.\r\n- **M2.** When one of the two is a transfer side, the kept transaction becomes that transfer side: the counterpart\r\n  stays, references the kept transaction, and nothing is added or deleted in the other account.\r\n- **M3.** After a merge, the kept transaction follows T5 and T6: if the other account is on-budget, it has no\r\n  category; if the other account is off-budget, it keeps the category.\r\n\r\n## B.
